````text
# #3751: Patch: follow-up to #3745 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3745 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3745 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43150457889)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`db28caaa66d0`). `claude-2` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3745 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `crates/ai/src/decide.rs:574`: R3696000's extra shortlisted line is replied to before the finalists are scored on the other determinizations, so on a short counter or clock it spends the nodes those worlds need. That contradicts the ruling note's claim that coming last means a counter that runs short drops it first, and the issue's plan to skip the extra place when the clock is short was never built.
  Evidence: In `plan` (decide.rs ~566-624), the `for line in shortlist { reply_score(...) }` loop runs to completion on det0, and only after it does `for world in dets.iter().skip(1) { score_line(...) }` run on the same `counter`. A world that cannot finish is dropped (`if row.len() < finalists.len() { break; }`), which lowers `worlds_scored` and makes `Decision::fell_short()` true (types.rs:185). The extra line is pushed past `count` in `shortlist_lines`, but `reserve` is still sized for `finalist_count * lines_per_action` replies (`per_finalist`, decide.rs ~519). A countdown line such as Supply Drop's also runs `simulate_reply` twice in `reply_score` (`countdowns_due`). So the extra reply comes out of the reserve meant for worlds 1..K-1. Yet spec/rulings/R3696000.md says 'and last, so a counter that runs short drops it first', and the PR says skipping on a short clock 'needs no code of its own'. Fix: reply to the extra line after the other worlds are scored, or only while the counter still covers their reserve, or add its reply to `reserve`. In each case correct the note and the §9.9 text to match, and add a test where a tight budget shows `worlds_scored` unchanged by the extra line.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

   let payoff = if out.iter().any(waits) {

   /// R3696000: the payoff line's score after the opponent's reply, drawn only on the nodes `counter` holds
   /// past `keep` (what the finalists' scores on every other determinization keep back), so it never takes
   /// one of theirs; `None` when those run out first.
   fn payoff_score(
       line: &Line,
       seat: PlayerId,
       root_turn: i32,
       counter: &dyn NodeCounter,
       keep: usize,
       hidden: &IndexSet<String>,
       prices: &Prices,
   ) -> Option<f64> {
       let spare = create_sub_counter(
           counter,
           counter.limit().saturating_sub(counter.used()).saturating_sub(keep),
       );
       reply_score(&line.end, seat, root_turn, &spare, hidden, prices)
   }
   ```

   // What one finalist's scores on every other determinization keep back (R3696000's `keep`, below).
   let other_worlds = (k - 1) * (budget.max_depth + 1 + AI_REPLY.reserve_steps as usize);

   - Directly after the loop, insert the block below. `wrap_up` is the `let wrap_up = options.wrap_up;` at the top of `plan`.
   ```rust
   // R3696000: the payoff line last, once every shortlisted line is replied to: skipped once the host's
   // clock has passed its wrap-up (R3498000), else replied to on the nodes past what the other worlds
   // keep back. Either stop, when it comes, is the decision's own.
   let mut payoff_stop: Option<StoppedBy> = None;
   if let Some(line) = payoff
       && replied.len() == shortlist.len()
   {
       if wrap_up.is_some_and(|wrapped| wrapped()) {
           payoff_stop = Some(StoppedBy::Clock);
       } else {
           match payoff_score(line, seat, root_turn, counter, finalist_count * other_worlds, &hidden0, &prices) {
               Some(score) => replied.push(Scored { line, score }),
               None => payoff_stop = Some(StoppedBy::Budget),
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   /// The shortlist's scores, the payoff line's last.

A host with a clock fires it at` / `/// `AI_WRAP_UP_SHARE` of its limit (`wrap_up_after_ms`).`

It is not replied to at all once a host's clock has passed its wrap-up ([[R3498000]]), which the search polls once before it. So a counter or a clock that runs short drops it first, and the decision's `stoppedBy` says which (`budget`, `clock`).

Replying to it after the other worlds are scored: the finalists are picked from determinization 0's replies, so it could then be weighed only on fewer worlds than they are, or played again on each world already scored. Checking the nodes left against an estimate and then replying on the whole counter: a reply longer than the estimate would still take theirs, which a slice cannot. **Tests**

New test in the tests module of `crates/ai/src/decide.rs`:
```rust
/// R3696000: `payoff_score` with exactly `keep` nodes left takes none of them and leaves the counter
/// running for the other worlds; with more left it is the line's `reply_score`.
#[test]
fn r3696000_the_payoff_line_is_replied_to_on_no_node_the_other_worlds_keep() {
    let root = board(true).state().clone();
    let Some(Ok(end)) = simulate(&root, AI, &ActionBody::EndTurn, &create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None), Prices::NONE) else {
        panic!("the AI ends its turn");
    };
    let line = Line { actions: vec![ActionBody::EndTurn], score: 0.0, status: LineStatus::Passed, end };
    let hidden = hidden_card_ids(&root, AI);
    let keep = 40;
    let tight = create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None);
    while tight.limit() - tight.used() > keep {
        assert!(tight.take());
    }
    assert_eq!(payoff_score(&line, AI, root.turn, &tight, keep, &hidden, Prices::NONE), None);
    assert_eq!(tight.used(), AI_BUDGET.nodes - keep);
    assert_eq!(tight.stopped_by(), StoppedBy::Exhausted);
    assert!(tight.take(), "the kept nodes are still the other worlds'");
    let plain = reply_score(&line.end, AI, root.turn, &create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None), &hidden, Prices::NONE);
    assert!(plain.is_some(), "PREMISE: the reply scores the line");
    let ample = create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None);
    assert_eq!(payoff_score(&line, AI, root.turn, &ample, keep, &hidden, Prices::NONE), plain);
    assert!(ample.used() > 0);
}
```
Two details:
- It must be `board(true)`. With `board(false)` the other side has nothing to do, so its turn passes inside `simulate` and the reply takes no node.
- `Prices::NONE` is already a `&Prices`, so writing `&Prices::NONE` fails clippy.

Changes to `crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`:
- Add `use std::cell::Cell;` above `use jackioh_ai::*;`.
- Just above `r3696000_the_ai_still_casts_supply_drop_in_combat_mode_with_two_castable_units_in_hand`, add `fn supply_drop_beside_two_vanillas() -> GameState` with the doc comment `/// R3696000: Supply Drop beside two castable Vanillas, against three Curvatures.` Its body is that test's `register_cards(); scenario(json!({…})).state().clone()`, verbatim.
- Make that test call the helper. Its assertions stay unchanged.
- Add `const SHORTLIST: usize = AI_BUDGET.finalists * AI_SEARCH.lines_per_action as usize;` with the doc comment `/// The lines `shortlist_lines` takes at the browser's budget, before the payoff line (R3696000).`
- Add these two tests:
  - `r3696000_on_a_tight_budget_the_supply_drop_line_costs_no_world_its_score`
    - For `nodes` in `(60..=200).step_by(5)`, decide with `AiOptions::with_budget(create_rng("ai-supply-drop-combat", 0), SearchBudget { nodes, ..AI_BUDGET })`, and collect the decisions.
    - For each decision, assert `stats.replied <= SHORTLIST || stats.worlds_scored == AI_BUDGET.determinizations`, with the stats' `{:?}` as the message.
    - Premise: some decision has `replied > SHORTLIST`.
    - Premise: some decision has `replied == SHORTLIST && worlds_scored == determinizations && stopped_by == StoppedBy::Budget`.
    - Measured on the fix: from 121 to 174 nodes it replies to 6 lines and scores 3 worlds; from 175 up it replies to 7 and scores 3. On `main`, from 99 to 134 it replies to 7 and scores fewer than 3.
  - `r3696000_past_the_wrap_up_the_supply_drop_line_is_not_replied_to`
    - Use `budget = SearchBudget { root_branching: AI_BUDGET.nodes, ..AI_BUDGET }`. The beam never reaches its wrap-up floor (`root_branching + 1` nodes), so the only poll is the search's own.
    - With no clock, `plain` gives `replied == SHORTLIST + 1` (PREMISE) and `stopped_by == Exhausted`.
    - Then decide with a wrap-up that always answers `true`, counting its polls in a `Cell`: `AiOptions { rng: create_rng("ai-supply-drop-combat", 0), budget, should_stop: None, wrap_up: Some(&fired) }`.
    - Assert `polls == 1`, `wrapped.stats.lines == plain.stats.lines` ("one beam"), `wrapped.stats.replied == SHORTLIST`, `worlds_scored == AI_BUDGET.determinizations` and `stopped_by == StoppedBy::Clock`.

```
cargo test -p jackioh-ai r3696000
cargo test -p jackioh-ai r3498000
cargo test -p jackioh-ai
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo jackioh spec check
```

**Done when**

- [ ] The payoff line is replied to after the shortlist, on its own sub-counter, and skipped past the wrap-up (steps 1–6).
- [ ] Its stop shows in `stoppedBy` (step 6).
- [ ] R3696000, R3498000, §9.9, the README, `types.rs` and `docs/polish/3-ai.md` say what the code does (steps 8–13).
- [ ] The three new tests and every existing `r3696000_*` and `r3498000_*` test pass, with no assertion weakened.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes.
- [ ] rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests are all green, and any red check is reported by name.

**Risks**

- **Decisions change, by design.** Wherever the reserve cannot spare the payoff line its reply, it is no longer replied to: fat states, the 150- and 300-node ladder bots, any budget-bound board.
  - With one determinization (`TEST_BUDGET`), `keep` is 0 and the slice holds everything left, so those decisions are the same node for node.
  - With no clock, nothing is polled.
  - The daily AI gates may move slightly: report what they show and do not tune them.
- **Determinism and replay.** There is no new random draw. The poll runs only with a clock, and the server never re-runs AI moves (R2560000).
- **Pinned decisions in other crates** (`crates/shared/tests/bots_decide.rs`, `crates/wasm/core`, `crates/tools`). The workspace tests were not run in the scratch copy. If one fails, check whether its decision held a payoff line that the new limit now drops. Report it, and never loosen its assertion to get green.
- **Hidden information.** Nothing new is read: `leaves_own_delayed` reads only the seat's own entries.
- **`spec check`.** The new tests carry the `r3696000` token, in files already in R3696000's `proven_in`. Do not name a test `r3498000_…` in `meditative_plus.rs`, which is not in R3498000's `proven_in`.

**Open questions**

None needs a person. The decisions taken, each with the alternative rejected:
- **(a)** The payoff line runs on a slice past the reserve's own measure of the other worlds. Rejected: replying to it after the other worlds are scored, which changes how finalists are picked; and a bigger reserve, which R3696000 already rejects.
- **(b)** The search polls the wrap-up once, before the payoff line. Rejected: reading `beam_stopped_by`, which misses a wrap-up that fires while the shortlist is being replied to.
- **(c)** A skipped or cut payoff line shows in `stoppedBy`. Rejected: leaving it `exhausted`, which would hide a budget or a clock that cut the search.
- **(d)** R3696000 is corrected in place. Rejected: a new R3751000 ruling, since the issue asks for the note to be corrected.
````
